blocks.p: The game itself shows what you carry in an inventory window and what is around you in a loot window. Each window shows one container at a time; to see another, click its button on the right edge of the window.

Figure 9-1 shows the two windows of the game itself, the inventory window at the left and the loot window at the right, each with its column of container buttons at its right edge. Only one container can be seen in each window.

caption: Figure 9-1
The game's own windows: inventory, left, and loot, right.

blocks.p: ZNIX shows the same things in two windows of its own, the *Character* window and the *World* window, and gives every open container a column of its own. Figure 9-2 on the facing page shows the same moment in ZNIX.

marks.text: Vanilla: an inventory window and a loot window. The buttons on the right edge pick a container.

sticky.text: The game's own: one container per window.

blocks.p: In ZNIX each open container sits beside the others as a column. The *Character* window holds what you carry: in Figure 9-2, the inventory. The *World* window holds what is in reach: here, the ground. The buttons beside the columns open the other containers, each in a column of its own.

caption: Figure 9-2
The same moment in ZNIX: the Character window, left, and the World window, right.

blocks.p: To move an item, drag it to another column. The item goes into the container of the column you drop it on.

marks.text: Character window: the inventory, in a column of its own.
World window: the ground. The buttons beside it open the other containers in reach.
The gas can's level, in blue cells.

sticky.text: In ZeD every container is a column.
